stimuli.title: Pitching Machine
stimuli.html:
A pitching machine at a batting cage launches a ball straight up into the air to test its power. The ball leaves the machine 6 feet above the ground. The height h of the ball, in feet, t seconds after it is launched is modeled by the function below.

h(t) = −16t2 + 48t + 6

Use this information to answer the questions that follow.

items.prompt:
What is the value of the expression below?

24 ÷ (2 − 6) + 3 × 23
items.explain:
Work inside the parentheses first: 2 − 6 = −4.

Exponent: 23 = 8.

Multiply and divide from left to right: 24 ÷ (−4) = −6 and 3 × 8 = 24.

Add: −6 + 24 = 18.

30 comes from treating 24 ÷ (−4) as +6. 210 comes from multiplying 3 × 2 before applying the exponent: 63 = 216, and −6 + 216 = 210. The exponent applies only to the 2.

items.prompt:
On a weekend trip, Jamal hiked 3½ miles in the morning and 2¾ miles in the afternoon. How many miles did he hike in all?

Write your answer as a fraction or a decimal.
items.explain:
Use a common denominator of 4: 3½ = 3&frac24;.

Add the whole numbers: 3 + 2 = 5.

Add the fractions: 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4 = 1¼.

Total: 5 + 1¼ = 6¼ miles (25/4 or 6.25).

A common error is to add the numerators and denominators separately: 1/2 + 3/4 is not 4/6. The fractions need a common denominator first.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (x4)3 ÷ x5 for x ≠ 0?
items.explain:
Power of a power: multiply the exponents. (x4)3 = x4 × 3 = x12.

Dividing powers with the same base: subtract the exponents. x12 ÷ x5 = x12 − 5 = x7.

x2 comes from adding 4 + 3 instead of multiplying, then subtracting 5. x17 adds the exponents when it should subtract them.

items.prompt:
What value of x makes the equation true?

(2/3)x − 4 = 10
items.explain:
Add 4 to both sides: (2/3)x = 14.

Multiply both sides by the reciprocal, 3/2: x = 14 × 3/2 = 42/2 = 21.

Check: (2/3)(21) − 4 = 14 − 4 = 10.

28/3 comes from multiplying 14 by 2/3 instead of dividing by 2/3. 9 comes from subtracting 4 instead of adding it (10 − 4 = 6, and 6 × 3/2 = 9).

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to −2(3x − 5) + 4x?
items.explain:
Distribute −2 to both terms in the parentheses: −2(3x) = −6x and −2(−5) = +10.

−6x + 10 + 4x

Combine like terms: −6x + 4x = −2x.

Result: −2x + 10.

−2x − 10 forgets that a negative times a negative is positive. −2x + 5 distributes the −2 to the 3x only.

items.prompt: A cyclist rode 54 miles in 3.6 hours at a steady pace. What was her average speed?
items.explain:
Speed = distance ÷ time.

54 ÷ 3.6 = 15 miles per hour.

Check: 15 × 3.6 = 54 miles.

194.4 multiplies instead of dividing. 0.07 divides time by distance (3.6 ÷ 54), which gives hours per mile, not miles per hour. 18 rounds the time down to 3 hours.

items.prompt: A fitness center raised its monthly membership fee from $40 to $46. By what percent did the fee increase?
items.explain:
Amount of increase: 46 − 40 = $6.

Percent increase = increase ÷ original amount = 6 ÷ 40 = 0.15 = 15%.

13% comes from dividing by the new fee (6 ÷ 46 ≈ 0.13). 6% treats the $6 increase as a percent. 115% is the new fee as a percent of the old fee, not the increase.

items.prompt: On a park trail map, 1 inch represents 0.75 mile. A loop trail measures 5.2 inches on the map. What is the actual length of the trail, in miles?
items.explain:
Each inch stands for 0.75 mile, so multiply:

5.2 × 0.75 = 3.9 miles.

As a proportion: 1/0.75 = 5.2/m, so m = 5.2 × 0.75 = 3.9.

Dividing (5.2 ÷ 0.75 ≈ 6.9) would make the real trail longer per inch than the scale allows.

items.prompt: A softball team has played 30 games and has no ties. The ratio of its wins to its losses is 7 : 3. How many more games has the team won than lost?
items.explain:
The ratio 7 : 3 has 7 + 3 = 10 parts.

Each part: 30 ÷ 10 = 3 games.

Wins: 7 × 3 = 21. Losses: 3 × 3 = 9.

Difference: 21 − 9 = 12 more wins than losses.

4 is the difference in the ratio (7 − 3) but not in actual games. 21 and 9 are the numbers of wins and losses, not the difference.

items.prompt: A football stadium has 6.5 × 104 seats. Every seat was filled for each of the team's 8 home games this season. What was the total home attendance for the season?
items.explain:
Multiply: 8 × (6.5 × 104) = 52 × 104.

Rewrite in scientific notation: 52 × 104 = 5.2 × 101 × 104 = 5.2 × 105 (520,000 people).

5.2 × 104 forgets to raise the exponent when 52 becomes 5.2. 8.125 × 103 divides by 8 instead of multiplying.

items.prompt:
A youth soccer coach recorded how many goals her team scored in each game of the season.

Goals scored in a game01234
Number of games25643

What was the mean number of goals the team scored per game? Write your answer as a decimal.
items.explain:
Total number of games: 2 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 3 = 20.

Total goals (goals × games for each column):

0 × 2 = 0; 1 × 5 = 5; 2 × 6 = 12; 3 × 4 = 12; 4 × 3 = 12

0 + 5 + 12 + 12 + 12 = 41 goals.

Mean = 41 ÷ 20 = 2.05 goals per game.

A common error is to average only the column headings, (0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4) ÷ 5 = 2, which ignores how many games each score happened.

items.prompt:
Seven swimmers recorded these times, in seconds, in a 100-meter freestyle race.

58.4, 61.2, 57.9, 60.5, 59.3, 62.0, 58.8

The median time is {{0}}.

The range of the times is {{1}}.
items.explain:
Put the times in order: 57.9, 58.4, 58.8, 59.3, 60.5, 61.2, 62.0.

With 7 values, the median is the 4th value: 59.3 seconds.

Range = greatest − least = 62.0 − 57.9 = 4.1 seconds.

60.5 is the middle of the list before it is put in order. 59.7 is the mean (418.1 ÷ 7 ≈ 59.73), not the median. 3.6 subtracts the first time listed (58.4) instead of the least time.

items.prompt: A basketball player makes 80% of her free throws. She shoots two free throws, and the results of the two shots are independent. What is the probability that she makes both free throws?
items.explain:
For independent events, multiply the probabilities:

P(make both) = 0.80 × 0.80 = 0.64 (64%).

1.60 adds the probabilities; a probability can never be greater than 1. 0.16 is 0.80 × 0.20, the probability of making the first shot and missing the second. 0.80 is the probability for just one shot.

items.prompt: A climbing team has 9 members. The coach will choose one member to be captain and a different member to be co-captain. How many different ways can the coach fill the two positions?
items.explain:
There are 9 choices for captain. Once the captain is chosen, 8 members remain for co-captain.

9 × 8 = 72 ways.

The order matters here: Ana as captain with Ben as co-captain is different from Ben as captain with Ana as co-captain.

81 (9 × 9) lets the same person hold both positions. 36 (72 ÷ 2) would be correct only if the two positions were the same, so order did not matter. 18 adds 9 + 9.

items.prompt: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 26 inches. One mile is 63,360 inches. About how many complete turns does the wheel make when the bicycle travels 1 mile? Round to the nearest whole number. Use the formula sheet if needed.
items.explain:
In one turn, the wheel rolls a distance equal to its circumference.

C = πd = π(26) ≈ 81.68 inches.

Number of turns = 63,360 ÷ 81.68 ≈ 775.7, which rounds to 776 turns.

2,437 divides by the diameter instead of the circumference. 1,551 uses πr = π(13), which is only half the circumference. 119 divides by the area of the wheel, π(13)2, which is not a distance.

items.prompt: The infield of a running track is shaped like a rectangle with a semicircle on each end, as shown. The rectangle is 100 meters long and 64 meters wide, and the diameter of each semicircle is 64 meters. To the nearest square meter, what is the area of the infield?

figure.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 190' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M80,40 L240,40 A51,51 0 0 1 240,142 L80,142 A51,51 0 0 1 80,40 Z' fill='#F3E9C9' stroke='#0A1F3D' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='80' y1='40' x2='80' y2='142' stroke='#0A1F3D' stroke-dasharray='5,4'/><line x1='240' y1='40' x2='240' y2='142' stroke='#0A1F3D' stroke-dasharray='5,4'/><text x='140' y='30' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>100 m</text><text x='246' y='96' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>64 m</text></svg>
figure.alt: A track infield made of a rectangle 100 meters long and 64 meters wide, with a semicircle attached to each 64-meter end. Dashed lines separate the semicircles from the rectangle.

items.explain:
Rectangle: 100 × 64 = 6,400 square meters.

The two semicircles together make one full circle with diameter 64 m, so the radius is 32 m.

Circle area: πr2 = π(32)2 = 1,024π ≈ 3,216.99 square meters.

Total: 6,400 + 3,216.99 ≈ 9,617 square meters.

8,008 counts only one semicircle. 19,268 uses 64 as the radius. 6,601 adds the circumference of the circle (2π × 32 ≈ 201) instead of its area.

items.prompt: A baseball diamond is a square with sides of 90 feet. A catcher throws the ball in a straight line from home plate to second base, which is the opposite corner of the square. How far is the throw, in feet? Round your answer to the nearest tenth.
items.explain:
The path from home plate to second base is the diagonal of the square. It is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with two legs of 90 feet.

c2 = 902 + 902 = 8,100 + 8,100 = 16,200

c = √16,200 ≈ 127.279

Rounded to the nearest tenth: 127.3 feet.

Adding the two sides (180 feet) gives the distance running along the base paths, not the straight throw.

items.skill: Volume of a cylinder with unit conversion
items.prompt: A round above-ground swimming pool is shaped like a cylinder with a diameter of 18 feet. It is filled with water to a depth of 4 feet. One cubic foot holds about 7.48 gallons of water. About how many gallons of water are in the pool? Use the formula sheet if needed.
items.explain:
Volume of a cylinder: V = πr2h. The radius is 18 ÷ 2 = 9 feet.

V = π(9)2(4) = π(81)(4) = 324π ≈ 1,017.88 cubic feet.

Convert to gallons: 1,017.88 × 7.48 ≈ 7,614 gallons.

1,018 is the volume in cubic feet, before converting to gallons. 30,455 uses the diameter, 18, as the radius. 136 divides by 7.48 instead of multiplying.

items.prompt: A basketball has a diameter of 9.4 inches. To the nearest tenth of a cubic inch, what is the volume of the ball? Use the formula sheet if needed.
items.explain:
Volume of a sphere: V = (4/3)πr3. The radius is 9.4 ÷ 2 = 4.7 inches.

r3 = 4.7 × 4.7 × 4.7 = 103.823

V = (4/3)π(103.823) ≈ 434.9 cubic inches.

3,479.1 uses the diameter as the radius. 1,304.7 leaves out the division by 3 (4πr3). 277.6 is 4πr2, the surface area, not the volume.

items.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
items.prompt: A closed storage box for gym equipment is a rectangular prism 4 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 1.5 feet tall. The outside of the box, including the lid and bottom, will be covered with vinyl. How many square feet of vinyl are needed? Use the formula sheet if needed.
items.explain:
Surface area of a rectangular prism: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh.

2lw = 2(4)(2) = 16

2lh = 2(4)(1.5) = 12

2wh = 2(2)(1.5) = 6

SA = 16 + 12 + 6 = 34 square feet.

A common error is to find the volume instead: 4 × 2 × 1.5 = 12 cubic feet. Covering the outside is a surface area question.

items.prompt: A pair of running shoes is regularly priced at $120. The store takes 30% off the regular price. At the register, a coupon takes an additional 10% off the sale price. What is the final price of the shoes, before tax?
items.explain:
First discount: 30% of $120 = 0.30 × 120 = $36, so the sale price is 120 − 36 = $84.00.

Second discount: 10% of $84 = $8.40, so the final price is 84.00 − 8.40 = $75.60.

Shortcut: 120 × 0.70 × 0.90 = 75.60.

$72.00 adds the discounts to get 40% off the regular price. That is wrong because the 10% is taken from the lower sale price, not from $120. $84.00 applies only the first discount.

items.prompt: Lena finished a 6.2-mile race in 52 minutes 42 seconds. What was her average pace, in time per mile?
items.explain:
Change the time to minutes: 42 seconds = 42/60 = 0.7 minute, so the time is 52.7 minutes.

Pace = time ÷ distance = 52.7 ÷ 6.2 = 8.5 minutes per mile.

Change 0.5 minute to seconds: 0.5 × 60 = 30 seconds. The pace is 8 minutes 30 seconds per mile.

8 minutes 27 seconds comes from writing 52 minutes 42 seconds as 52.42 minutes. 8 minutes 5 seconds misreads 8.5 minutes as 8 minutes 5 seconds. 8 minutes 47 seconds divides by 6 miles instead of 6.2.

items.prompt: A square boxing ring has an area of 484 square feet. Three rows of rope run around all four sides of the ring. What is the total length of rope needed, in feet?
items.explain:
Side length of the square: s = √484 = 22 feet.

Perimeter of the ring: 4 × 22 = 88 feet.

Three rows of rope: 3 × 88 = 264 feet.

88 is the length of only one row. 66 is three sides’ worth of one row (3 × 22). 1,452 multiplies the area by 3, which mixes square feet with feet.

items.prompt: Drag each number into the correct position to order the numbers from least to greatest.
items.explain:
Write each number as a decimal:

3/100 = 0.03; 3.2 × 10−2 = 0.032; 1/30 ≈ 0.0333; 2.9 × 10−1 = 0.29; 0.3

Order from least to greatest: 3/100, 3.2 × 10−2, 1/30, 2.9 × 10−1, 0.3.

A negative exponent moves the decimal point to the left, so 3.2 × 10−2 is small (0.032), not 320. Also, 1/30 is about 0.0333, slightly greater than 0.032.

items.prompt: Gym A charges a $50 joining fee plus $25 per month. Gym B has no joining fee and charges $35 per month. After how many months will the total cost be the same at both gyms?
items.explain:
Let m be the number of months.

Gym A: 50 + 25m. Gym B: 35m.

Set the costs equal: 50 + 25m = 35m

Subtract 25m from both sides: 50 = 10m

m = 5 months

Check: Gym A costs 50 + 25(5) = $175, and Gym B costs 35(5) = $175.

Dividing 50 by 35 (about 1.4) ignores the monthly fee at Gym A. The costs become equal because Gym B costs $10 more each month, and that makes up the $50 fee after 5 months.

items.prompt: A trainer uses the formula T = 0.7(220 − a) to estimate a target heart rate T, in beats per minute, for a person who is a years old. What is the target heart rate for a 40-year-old?
items.explain:
Substitute a = 40:

T = 0.7(220 − 40) = 0.7(180) = 126 beats per minute.

114 comes from multiplying 0.7 × 220 = 154 first and then subtracting 40. The subtraction inside the parentheses must be done first. 180 forgets to multiply by 0.7.

items.prompt: The distance around a running track with straight sides of length l and semicircular ends of diameter d is given by P = 2l + πd. Which equation correctly solves this formula for l?
items.explain:
Start with P = 2l + πd.

Subtract πd from both sides: P − πd = 2l.

Divide both sides by 2: l = (P − πd) / 2.

l = P/2 − πd divides only P by 2; the πd term must also be divided by 2. l = (P + πd) / 2 adds πd instead of subtracting it.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (x + 4)(x2 − 2x + 3)?
items.explain:
Multiply each term of (x + 4) by each term of the trinomial.

x(x2 − 2x + 3) = x3 − 2x2 + 3x

4(x2 − 2x + 3) = 4x2 − 8x + 12

Combine like terms: x3 + (−2x2 + 4x2) + (3x − 8x) + 12 = x3 + 2x2 − 5x + 12.

x3 + 2x2 + 11x + 12 uses +8x instead of 4(−2x) = −8x. x3 − 2x2 + 3x + 12 leaves out the middle products 4x2 and −8x.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to x2 − 10x + 21?
items.explain:
Find two numbers that multiply to +21 and add to −10. Both numbers must be negative: −3 and −7, because (−3)(−7) = 21 and −3 + (−7) = −10.

x2 − 10x + 21 = (x − 3)(x − 7).

Check: (x − 3)(x − 7) = x2 − 7x − 3x + 21 = x2 − 10x + 21.

(x + 3)(x + 7) gives x2 + 10x + 21, which has the wrong sign on the middle term. (x − 3)(x + 7) gives a constant of −21.

items.prompt: The expression 3x2 − 48 can be factored completely as 3 times two binomials. Which binomials are factors of 3x2 − 48? Select two answers.
items.explain:
First factor out the greatest common factor, 3: 3x2 − 48 = 3(x2 − 16).

x2 − 16 is a difference of squares: x2 − 42 = (x − 4)(x + 4).

So 3x2 − 48 = 3(x − 4)(x + 4).

Check: 3(x2 + 4x − 4x − 16) = 3(x2 − 16) = 3x2 − 48.

x − 16 and x + 16 forget to take the square root of 16. 3x − 16 divides only one term by 3.

items.prompt: Rosa is planning a family reunion with a budget of $520. She has already paid $140 to rent a park pavilion. Each catered food tray costs $45. What is the greatest number of food trays she can order and stay within her budget?
items.explain:
Let t be the number of trays: 140 + 45t ≤ 520.

Subtract 140: 45t ≤ 380.

Divide by 45: t ≤ 8.44…

She cannot order part of a tray, and rounding up would go over budget, so the greatest number is 8 trays.

Check: 140 + 45(8) = $500, which is within budget; 140 + 45(9) = $545, which is over.

9 rounds 8.44 up. 11 ignores the $140 already spent (520 ÷ 45 ≈ 11.6).

items.prompt: Which inequality is equivalent to 5 − 2x ≤ 3x + 20?
items.explain:
Subtract 3x from both sides: 5 − 5x ≤ 20.

Subtract 5 from both sides: −5x ≤ 15.

Divide both sides by −5 and reverse the inequality sign: x ≥ −3.

Check with x = 0: 5 − 0 = 5 and 3(0) + 20 = 20, and 5 ≤ 20 is true. Since 0 ≥ −3, this agrees.

x ≤ −3 forgets to reverse the sign when dividing by a negative number.

items.prompt: At a high school basketball game, the concession stand sold hot dogs for $4 each and soft pretzels for $3 each. The stand sold 85 items in all and collected $295. How many pretzels were sold?
items.explain:
Let h = hot dogs and p = pretzels.

h + p = 85

4h + 3p = 295

From the first equation, h = 85 − p. Substitute:

4(85 − p) + 3p = 295

340 − 4p + 3p = 295

340 − p = 295, so p = 45 pretzels (and h = 40 hot dogs).

Check: 4(40) + 3(45) = 160 + 135 = $295.

40 is the number of hot dogs. 74 comes from 295 ÷ 4, which assumes every item was a hot dog.

items.prompt: The graphs of y = −x + 3 and y = 2x − 6 are shown on the coordinate plane. Click the point that represents the solution to the system of equations.
items.explain:
The solution is the point where the two lines cross. Set the expressions equal:

−x + 3 = 2x − 6

9 = 3x, so x = 3

y = −3 + 3 = 0

The solution is (3, 0). Check in the second equation: 2(3) − 6 = 0.

The y-intercepts (0, 3) and (0, −6) each lie on only one of the lines, so they are not solutions to the system.

items.prompt: Click the point on the coordinate plane that is the vertex of the graph of y = x2 − 4x + 1.
items.explain:
For y = ax2 + bx + c, the x-coordinate of the vertex is x = −b / (2a).

Here a = 1 and b = −4, so x = −(−4) / (2 × 1) = 4/2 = 2.

Find y: y = (2)2 − 4(2) + 1 = 4 − 8 + 1 = −3.

The vertex is (2, −3).

Another way: complete the square. x2 − 4x + 1 = (x − 2)2 − 4 + 1 = (x − 2)2 − 3, so the vertex is (2, −3).

The point (0, 1) is the y-intercept, not the vertex. Using x = b / (2a) = −2 gives the wrong side of the graph.

items.skill: Rate of change from a table
items.prompt:
A hiking group climbs a mountain trail at a steady rate. The table shows the group’s elevation E, in feet, t hours after starting.

Time t (hours)0246
Elevation E (feet)2,4003,3004,2005,100

The group climbs at a rate of {{0}} feet per hour.

The group started at an elevation of {{1}} feet.

After 5 hours, the group’s elevation is {{2}} feet.
items.explain:
Rate of change: the elevation rises 900 feet every 2 hours (2,400 to 3,300). 900 ÷ 2 = 450 feet per hour. Choosing 900 forgets that each step in the table is 2 hours, not 1.

Starting elevation: the value when t = 0 is 2,400 feet.

The model is E = 2,400 + 450t. After 5 hours: E = 2,400 + 450(5) = 2,400 + 2,250 = 4,650 feet.

2,250 is only the height gained in 5 hours; it leaves out the starting elevation.

items.skill: Equation of a line through two points
items.prompt: Which equation represents the line that passes through the points (−2, 7) and (4, −2)?
items.explain:
Slope: m = (−2 − 7) / (4 − (−2)) = −9/6 = −3/2.

Find b using (−2, 7): 7 = (−3/2)(−2) + b, so 7 = 3 + b and b = 4.

The equation is y = −(3/2)x + 4.

Check with (4, −2): −(3/2)(4) + 4 = −6 + 4 = −2.

y = −(3/2)x + 10 comes from a sign error: (−3/2)(−2) is +3, not −3. y = (3/2)x + 10 loses the negative sign on the slope. y = −(2/3)x + 17/3 uses change in x over change in y for the slope.

items.prompt: A lake rental shop uses the equation C = 15 + 8h to find the cost C, in dollars, of renting a kayak for h hours. What does the number 8 represent?
options: The one-time fee charged for every rental
The total cost of a 1-hour rental
The cost for each hour of the rental
The number of hours the kayak is rented
items.explain:
In C = 15 + 8h, the number 8 is multiplied by h, the number of hours. Each additional hour adds $8 to the cost, so 8 is the cost for each hour (the slope, or rate of change).

The 15 is the one-time fee (the y-intercept), because it is charged even when h = 0.

The total cost of a 1-hour rental is 15 + 8(1) = $23, not $8.

items.prompt: The function f is defined as f(x) = 4x − 9. For what value of x is f(x) = 15?
items.explain:
Set the function equal to 15: 4x − 9 = 15.

Add 9 to both sides: 4x = 24.

Divide by 4: x = 6.

Check: f(6) = 4(6) − 9 = 24 − 9 = 15.

A common error is to find f(15) instead: 4(15) − 9 = 51. The question gives the output, 15, and asks for the input.

items.prompt:
Two cyclists ride on the same road in the same direction at steady speeds.

Cyclist A’s distance from the starting line, in miles, after t hours is d = 14t.

Cyclist B’s distance from the starting line is shown in the table.

Time t (hours)0123
Distance d (miles)5172941

The faster rider is {{0}}.

At t = 0, Cyclist B is {{1}} ahead of the starting line.

Cyclist A catches up to Cyclist B after {{2}}.

options: neither; they ride at the same speed

items.explain:
Cyclist A’s speed is the slope of d = 14t: 14 miles per hour.

Cyclist B’s speed is the rate of change in the table: 17 − 5 = 12 miles each hour. So Cyclist A is faster.

At t = 0, Cyclist B’s distance is 5 miles, so B has a 5-mile head start. B’s equation is d = 12t + 5.

Set the distances equal: 14t = 12t + 5, so 2t = 5 and t = 2.5 hours.

Check: A: 14(2.5) = 35 miles. B: 12(2.5) + 5 = 35 miles.

Choosing Cyclist B because its table numbers are larger confuses distance with speed; B is ahead only because of its head start.

items.prompt: To the nearest hundredth of a second, how long after it is launched does the ball hit the ground? Use the formula sheet if needed.
items.explain:
The ball hits the ground when h(t) = 0: −16t2 + 48t + 6 = 0.

Use the quadratic formula with a = −16, b = 48, c = 6.

b2 − 4ac = 482 − 4(−16)(6) = 2,304 + 384 = 2,688

√2,688 ≈ 51.846

t = (−48 ± 51.846) / (2 × −16) = (−48 ± 51.846) / (−32)

t = (−48 − 51.846) / (−32) = −99.846 / −32 ≈ 3.12 seconds

The other solution, (−48 + 51.846) / (−32) ≈ −0.12, is negative, so it does not make sense for time. 3.00 seconds is when h = 6 (the ball returns to launch height), not ground level. 1.50 seconds is when the ball reaches its highest point.

items.prompt: What is the maximum height the ball reaches?
items.explain:
The maximum occurs at the vertex, t = −b / (2a) = −48 / (2 × −16) = −48 / −32 = 1.5 seconds.

h(1.5) = −16(1.5)2 + 48(1.5) + 6

(1.5)2 = 2.25, and −16(2.25) = −36

48(1.5) = 72

h(1.5) = −36 + 72 + 6 = 42 feet

54 feet comes from forgetting to square 1.5 (−16 × 1.5 = −24). 78 feet comes from leaving out the −16t2 term (72 + 6). 6 feet is the launch height.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 3/x + 2/(x + 1) for all values of x where the expression is defined?
items.explain:
The common denominator is x(x + 1) = x2 + x.

Rewrite each fraction: 3/x = 3(x + 1) / [x(x + 1)] = (3x + 3) / [x(x + 1)] and 2/(x + 1) = 2x / [x(x + 1)].

Add the numerators: (3x + 3 + 2x) / [x(x + 1)] = (5x + 3)/(x2 + x).

Check with x = 1: 3/1 + 2/2 = 4, and (5 + 3)/(1 + 1) = 8/2 = 4.

5/(2x + 1) adds the numerators and the denominators separately, which is never allowed. (5x + 1)/(x2 + x) multiplies only the x by 3 in 3(x + 1).

items.skill: Slope of a line from its equation
items.prompt: Drag each equation into the category that describes the slope of its graph.
items.explain:
y = 4 is a horizontal line: zero slope.

x = −2 is a vertical line: undefined slope.

y = −3x + 1 has slope −3: negative.

2x − y = 5 becomes y = 2x − 5, slope 2: positive.

3x + 4y = 8 becomes 4y = −3x + 8, so y = −(3/4)x + 2, slope −3/4: negative.

y − 6 = 2x becomes y = 2x + 6, slope 2: positive.

A common mistake is to read the slope of 2x − y = 5 as −2 without solving for y first; the −y flips the sign.

items.prompt: Which equations represent lines that are parallel to the line y = (2/3)x − 4? Select two answers.
items.explain:
Parallel lines have the same slope, 2/3, and different y-intercepts.

y = (2/3)x + 5 has slope 2/3 and y-intercept 5: parallel.

2x − 3y = 9: −3y = −2x + 9, so y = (2/3)x − 3. Slope 2/3, different intercept: parallel.

3x − 2y = 4 gives y = (3/2)x − 2 (slope 3/2). y = −(3/2)x + 1 has the negative reciprocal slope, so it is perpendicular. 2x + 3y = 6 gives y = −(2/3)x + 2 (slope −2/3). y = 3x − 2 has slope 3. None of these are parallel.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (6x5y−2) / (2x2y3) for x ≠ 0 and y ≠ 0?
items.explain:
Divide the coefficients: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

Subtract exponents for x: x5 − 2 = x3.

Subtract exponents for y: y−2 − 3 = y−5 = 1/y5.

Result: 3x3 / y5.

3x3y comes from treating the y exponent as −2 − (−3) = 1, a sign error. 4x3/y5 subtracts the coefficients instead of dividing them. 12x7y multiplies instead of dividing.
